title: Pre-eclampsia
diseaseDescription: Pre-eclampsia: new-onset hypertension in pregnancy with proteinuria or maternal end-organ involvement. This bounded map covers maternal KIR/fetal HLA-C genetics, uterine NK cells and defective spiral artery remodelling, placental ischaemia/oxidative stress, the antiangiogenic sFlt-1/soluble endoglin/PlGF axis and fetal FLT1 locus, AT1 receptor autoantibodies, complement and TNF-alpha, maternal endothelial dysfunction, and renal (endotheliosis, podocyte injury), HELLP, eclampsia/PRES and fetal growth restriction associations. Many mechanistic links rest on in vitro, rodent or primate models. Chronic hypertension without pre-eclampsia, gestational hypertension alone, postpartum-onset disease, screening test performance, long-term maternal cardiovascular outcomes and therapies are out of scope.
releaseNote: Initial bounded pre-eclampsia candidate from 30 primary reports (Europe PMC abstracts only). Associations, in-vitro mechanisms and animal-model findings remain distinct; qualifying and contradicting results are retained (weaker angiogenic alterations in late-onset disease, endotheliosis in normotensive pregnancy, AT1-AA in normotensive controls, isolated HELLP and term eclampsia with normal angiogenic profiles, population-specific KIR effects, non-attenuated FMD). Source checks were performed by agents, not humans. Independent domain review is pending; all scores are unassessed; no therapies are curated.

entities.label: Soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1)
entities.description: Circulating soluble splice variant of VEGF receptor 1 (FLT1) released by the placenta; binds and sequesters VEGF-A and PlGF.

entities.label: Soluble endoglin
entities.description: Placenta-derived soluble TGF-beta co-receptor (CD105 ectodomain) with antiangiogenic activity in the maternal circulation.

entities.label: Placental growth factor (PlGF)
entities.description: Proangiogenic VEGF-family growth factor of placental origin; its free circulating level falls in pre-eclampsia.

entities.label: Fetal FLT1 locus variant
entities.description: Variants in the fetal/placental genome near FLT1 (e.g. the rs4769613 enhancer variant) associated with pre-eclampsia risk.

entities.label: Placental ischaemia / hypoxia
entities.description: Reduced uteroplacental perfusion and low oxygen tension in the placenta.

entities.label: Maternal hypertension
entities.description: New-onset raised maternal blood pressure in pregnancy.

entities.label: HELLP syndrome
entities.description: Haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets complicating pre-eclampsia.

entities.label: Pre-eclampsia (clinical syndrome)
entities.description: Pregnancy-specific hypertensive syndrome with proteinuria or other maternal end-organ dysfunction after 20 weeks.

entities.label: Glomerular endotheliosis
entities.description: Swelling of glomerular endothelial cells with loss of fenestrae and capillary-lumen occlusion; the classic renal lesion of pre-eclampsia.

entities.label: Podocyte injury
entities.description: Glomerular podocyte damage and detachment, measured clinically as podocyturia (urinary shedding of podocytes) or urinary podocyte-specific proteins/mRNA (e.g. podocin, nephrin).

entities.label: Proteinuria
entities.description: Abnormal urinary protein excretion, a defining renal manifestation of pre-eclampsia.

entities.label: Eclampsia / cerebral involvement
entities.description: Generalised seizures and related cerebral involvement in a woman with pre-eclampsia.

entities.label: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
entities.description: Clinico-radiological syndrome of acute neurological symptoms with reversible, predominantly posterior subcortical vasogenic brain oedema on imaging; a common cerebral imaging correlate of eclampsia.

entities.label: Fetal growth restriction
entities.description: Failure of the fetus to reach its growth potential, frequently of placental origin.

entities.label: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor agonistic autoantibodies
entities.description: Agonistic IgG autoantibodies directed at the second extracellular loop of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor, detected in the circulation of women with pre-eclampsia.

entities.label: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor
entities.description: G-protein-coupled receptor for angiotensin II (AGTR1) expressed on vascular smooth muscle, trophoblast and endothelium; target of AT1-AA agonistic autoantibodies.

entities.label: Complement activation
entities.description: Activation of the complement cascade, including the alternative pathway (fragment Bb) and the terminal pathway (C5a, C5b-9), during pregnancy.

entities.label: TNF-alpha
entities.description: Pro-inflammatory cytokine tumour necrosis factor alpha, raised in the maternal circulation in pre-eclampsia and used to induce pre-eclampsia-like phenotypes in animals.

entities.label: Endothelin-1
entities.description: Potent endothelium-derived vasoconstrictor peptide acting through ETA/ETB receptors.

entities.label: Nitric oxide bioavailability
entities.description: Availability of endothelium-derived nitric oxide, reduced when the endogenous eNOS inhibitor asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) accumulates.

entities.label: Maternal endothelial dysfunction
entities.description: Impaired endothelium-dependent vasodilatation and activation of the maternal endothelium, assessed clinically by brachial artery flow-mediated dilation.

entities.label: Maternal KIR / fetal HLA-C genotype combination
entities.description: Combinations of maternal killer immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) haplotypes (notably KIR AA, lacking most activating KIR) with fetal HLA-C group alleles (C1/C2) expressed by invading extravillous trophoblast.
synonyms: KIR AA genotype with fetal HLA-C2
maternal KIR / fetal HLA-C ligand pair

entities.label: Uterine natural killer cells
entities.description: Decidual/uterine NK cells at the maternal-fetal interface that recognise trophoblast HLA-C via KIR and secrete factors influencing trophoblast behaviour.

entities.label: Extravillous trophoblast
entities.description: Invasive fetal trophoblast that migrates into decidua and myometrium and transforms maternal spiral arteries.

entities.label: Spiral artery remodelling
entities.description: Physiological transformation of maternal uterine spiral arteries into wide, low-resistance utero-placental vessels; defective remodelling corresponds to inhibition of this process.

entities.label: Placental oxidative stress
entities.description: Excess reactive oxygen species and oxidative damage within placental tissue.

claims.text: Placental sFlt-1, an antagonist of VEGF-A and PlGF, is upregulated in pre-eclamptic placentas with correspondingly raised systemic sFlt-1 levels that fall after delivery.
limitations: Cross-sectional comparison; cannot establish temporal order from this analysis alone
Sample size, case definition and assay details not given in the abstract
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: Exogenous sFlt-1 given to pregnant rats produces hypertension together with proteinuria and glomerular endotheliosis, reproducing the maternal phenotype of pre-eclampsia.
limitations: Animal model (pregnant rat sFlt-1 overexpression), not human pre-eclampsia
Supraphysiological sFlt-1 exposure; dose and kinetics not stated in abstract
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: In a nested case-control study of nulliparous women, serum sFlt-1 rose about five weeks before the clinical onset of pre-eclampsia, so the increase precedes the syndrome.
limitations: Observational nested case-control design; no intervention on sFlt-1
Healthy nulliparous trial population may not generalise to all pregnancies
Key effect sizes in the abstract are destroyed by the pipeline's HTML-stripping defect (text after 'P<0.001' is lost)
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: Reduced circulating free PlGF, alongside increased sFlt-1, precedes and predicts the later development of pre-eclampsia in nulliparous women.
limitations: Observational; prediction is not evidence of causation
Prediction performance and gestational-age-specific estimates not extractable because the abstract text after 'P<0.001' is lost to the HTML-stripping defect
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: Reduced oxygen tension selectively increases sFlt-1 mRNA and sFlt-1 secretion in primary human cytotrophoblasts, but not in umbilical vein endothelial cells or villous fibroblasts, linking placental hypoxia to antiangiogenic output.
limitations: In vitro primary trophoblast culture; oxygen tensions and culture conditions do not reproduce the in vivo placenta
No pre-eclamptic tissue or clinical outcome measured
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: Soluble endoglin administered to pregnant rats causes vascular permeability and hypertension, and when co-administered with sFlt-1 produces a severe pre-eclampsia phenotype including HELLP and fetal growth restriction.
limitations: Animal model (pregnant rat sEng/sFlt-1 overexpression), not human pre-eclampsia
Two-agent overexpression at non-physiological levels; relative contribution of sEng alone to HELLP not isolated
Journal published an erratum for this article (Nat Med 2006;12(7):862); corrected content not inspected
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: Circulating soluble endoglin rises two to three months before the clinical onset of pre-eclampsia and, together with a rising sFlt-1:PlGF ratio, marks women who later develop the syndrome.
limitations: Observational nested case-control design; association only
Preterm versus term contrasts and significance values in the abstract are lost to the pipeline's HTML-stripping defect ('<37 weeks', 'P<0.001')
Journal published an erratum for this article (N Engl J Med 2006;355(17):1840); corrected content not inspected
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: The placental (fetal-genome) C allele of the FLT1 enhancer variant rs4769613 is associated with pre-eclampsia in two Estonian cohorts, replicating the fetal-genome GWAS signal near FLT1; maternal and paternal genotypes were not associated.
limitations: Small numbers of pre-eclampsia cases; per-cohort associations only nominally significant
Single-population (Estonian) replication; effect size may not transfer to other ancestries
Odds-ratio text in the abstract is partly destroyed by the HTML-stripping defect around 'P<0.05'
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: In a prospective cohort of 3968 mother-child pairs, fetal-genome variants from the pre-eclampsia GWAS, including FLT1 enhancer SNPs, were associated with higher maternal serum sFLT1 and sFLT1:PlGF at 36 weeks and a steeper third-trimester rise, with effects specific to or stronger in the fetal genome.
limitations: Genotype-biomarker associations, not a pre-eclampsia outcome analysis
Single cohort; variant-level effect sizes not given in the abstract
Maternal polygenic score showed the opposite (lower first-trimester sFLT1) direction, so the genotype-sFLT1 relationship is gestation- and genome-dependent
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: Both early- and late-onset pre-eclampsia show raised plasma sFlt-1 and reduced PlGF, but the angiogenic-factor disturbance is markedly less pronounced in late-onset (term) disease, qualifying the antiangiogenic axis as a uniform explanation.
limitations: Cross-sectional, single-centre, small group sizes (not stated in abstract)
Early- and late-onset groups are compared with different gestational-age controls
Fold-change values are lost to the HTML-stripping defect around 'P<.001'
Abstract only; full text not inspected

claims.text: In a prospective controlled antepartum renal biopsy series, glomerular endotheliosis was present in every woman with pre-eclampsia (and also in every woman with gestational hypertension).
limitations: Small single-centre series
Lesion also found in gestational hypertension, so not specific to proteinuric PE
Cross-sectional; cannot establish temporal or causal relation

claims.text: The same biopsy series found endotheliosis in 5 of 12 normotensive pregnant controls and in non-proteinuric gestational hypertension; the authors conclude the lesion is not pathognomonic for pre-eclampsia, differing between groups mainly in degree.
limitations: Only 12 controls
Grading of degree is semi-quantitative
Biopsy timing near term may favour finding mild endotheliosis in normal pregnancy

claims.text: In a prospective cohort, podocyturia (podocin-positive cultured urinary cells) at ~27 weeks was present in all women who later developed pre-eclampsia and in none of the normotensive or gestational-hypertension women, i.e. podocyte shedding preceded clinical disease and proteinuria.
limitations: Only 15 pre-eclampsia cases
Nested matched subsample analysed rather than whole cohort
Podocyturia is a marker of podocyte loss; does not show it causes PE

claims.text: In women with pre-eclampsia, urinary soluble nephrin tracked proteinuria and urinary podocyte-specific mRNA (podocin, nephrin), suggesting proteinuria is accompanied by renal podocyte loss.
limitations: Very small number of PE women (n=9)
Correlational; cannot order podocyte loss and proteinuria causally
Repeated samples per woman

claims.text: In a gestational-age-matched retrospective cohort, sFlt-1/PlGF ratios were highest in pre-eclampsia complicated by HELLP syndrome compared with isolated PE and isolated HELLP.
limitations: Retrospective observational design
Ratio (sFlt-1/PlGF) rather than sFlt-1 alone
No normotensive control group in the comparison

claims.text: Isolated HELLP syndrome without hypertension/proteinuria showed the lowest sFlt-1 and sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, suggesting HELLP is not uniformly driven by the antiangiogenic state and may be a partly distinct entity.
limitations: Only 7 isolated HELLP cases
Retrospective
Single centre

claims.text: Women with preterm eclampsia had a more severe antiangiogenic state (lower PlGF and lower PlGF/sFlt-1 ratio) than women with severe pre-eclampsia; the difference was not seen at term.
limitations: Cross-sectional; samples at diagnosis
Small eclampsia subgroups (20 preterm, 15 term)
Association with low PlGF/ratio, not a test of causation

claims.text: About one-third of women with term eclampsia had a normal angiogenic profile, so eclampsia (cerebral involvement) can occur without the circulating antiangiogenic imbalance, especially at term.
limitations: Only 15 term eclampsia cases
Single time point at diagnosis

claims.text: In women with severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia undergoing brain imaging, eclampsia was the independent predictor of PRES (vasogenic subcortical oedema), present in 9 of 12 eclamptic women.
limitations: Retrospective, single centre, small sample
Imaging-indication selection bias
Wide confidence interval for the odds ratio

claims.text: In a prospective study, early-onset intrauterine growth restriction (as well as early-onset PE) showed lower PlGF and higher sFlt-1 than controls, pointing to a shared placental disorder, though changes were more pronounced in pre-eclampsia.
limitations: Cross-sectional sampling at diagnosis
Small subgroups once split by onset
Association only; marker levels may reflect placental size/damage

claims.text: In a case-control comparison of 25 pre-eclamptic women with 12 normotensive pregnant women and 10 pregnant women with essential hypertension, circulating immunoglobulin with agonistic activity at the AT1 receptor was detected in every pre-eclamptic patient and in none of the controls, and the activity fell after delivery.
limitations: Small single-centre case-control series with no gestational-age-matched longitudinal sampling, so antibody detection cannot be timed relative to disease onset
Detection relies on a bioassay in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes rather than a standardised human assay, and bioassay cut-offs are operator-defined
Cross-sectional design cannot separate cause from consequence of established pre-eclampsia

claims.text: The stimulatory activity of pre-eclamptic patient IgG was abolished by peptides corresponding to the second extracellular loop of the AT1 receptor, indicating that the autoantibodies act as direct epitope-specific agonists at the AT1 receptor in vitro (effect blocked by the protein kinase C inhibitor calphostin C).
limitations: Rat cardiomyocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells, not human uteroplacental or maternal vascular tissue
Demonstrates receptor agonism in culture only; no in vivo confirmation in this study
No quantification of how receptor occupancy relates to circulating antibody titre in patients

claims.text: Passive transfer of total IgG or affinity-purified AT1-AA from women with pre-eclampsia into pregnant mice reproduced hypertension, proteinuria, glomerular endotheliosis, placental abnormalities and reduced fetal size, and these features were prevented by the AT1 receptor antagonist losartan or by a neutralising epitope-peptide antibody; this is a mouse passive-transfer model, not human pre-eclampsia.
limitations: Mouse passive-transfer model; murine placentation and the mouse renin-angiotensin system differ from human pregnancy, so this is not human pre-eclampsia
IgG doses and exposure timing are experimentally imposed and may exceed physiological titres
Abstract reports no group sizes or effect magnitudes, and the phenotype is defined by surrogate features rather than clinical diagnostic criteria

claims.text: In a prospective gestational-age-matched nested case-control study (30 pre-eclamptic, 30 normotensive pregnant women) AT1-AA were detected in only 70% of pre-eclamptic women and were also present in about 20% of normotensive pregnant controls, sFlt-1 discriminated better overall, and AT1-AA performed best for late-onset rather than early-onset disease.
limitations: Small sample (30 per group) limits precision of prevalence estimates and of the early- versus late-onset subgroup contrast
AT1-AA bioassay positivity is threshold-dependent, so the 20% control positivity rate may be assay-specific
Case-control sampling at or near diagnosis cannot establish temporal precedence

claims.text: In a gestational-age- and parity-matched case-control study (25 severe pre-eclampsia, 25 chronic hypertension, 25 healthy pregnant controls), urinary excretion of the terminal complement complex C5b-9 was present in nearly all women with severe pre-eclampsia but almost absent in both control groups, with C3a and C5a also raised in urine, indicating complement dysregulation in severe pre-eclampsia beyond that of hypertensive pregnancy generally.
limitations: Cross-sectional sampling at enrolment in established severe disease, so complement activation cannot be timed relative to onset
Urinary complement excretion may partly reflect proteinuria and glomerular filtration of plasma proteins rather than local activation
Small single-centre sample restricted to severe pre-eclampsia; mild and late-onset phenotypes untested

claims.text: In 86 women assessed at 23-25 weeks' gestation, brachial artery flow-mediated dilation was markedly lower in the ten women who later developed pre-eclampsia than in women with normal outcome, so impaired maternal endothelial function is detectable before the clinical syndrome appears.
limitations: Only ten women developed pre-eclampsia, so the estimate is imprecise and subtype-specific effects cannot be examined
Cohort enriched for abnormal uterine artery Doppler, limiting generalisability to unselected pregnancies
Flow-mediated dilation is operator-dependent and an indirect surrogate for endothelial nitric oxide function

claims.text: Plasma concentrations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, the endogenous inhibitor of endothelial nitric oxide synthase and therefore a marker of reduced nitric oxide bioavailability, were raised in women with impaired placental perfusion and were associated with impaired endothelial function in some women, which the authors read as a potential contributory factor for pre-eclampsia.
limitations: ADMA is an indirect proxy for nitric oxide bioavailability; nitric oxide itself was not measured
The ADMA elevation tracked impaired placental perfusion irrespective of outcome, so it is not specific to pre-eclampsia
The ADMA-flow-mediated-dilation correlation was confined to the small subgroup who developed pre-eclampsia and is therefore fragile

claims.text: In a small study of 32 normal and 28 hypertensive or pre-eclamptic pregnancies, brachial artery flow-mediated dilation in the third trimester was not reduced (indeed numerically greater) in hypertensive pregnancies despite raised hsCRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha, and no inflammatory marker correlated with flow-mediated dilation, contradicting a uniform brachial endothelial deficit in hypertensive pregnancy.
limitations: Hypertensive disorders and pre-eclampsia are pooled in one group, so a pre-eclampsia-specific deficit could be masked
Very small sample (n=60) and non-significant group differences; underpowered for a null claim
Single late-gestation measurement in a low-profile journal, with no correction for antihypertensive treatment

claims.text: Chronic infusion of purified AT1-AA into normal pregnant rats raised mean arterial pressure and increased renal cortical and placental endothelin-1, and the hypertension was abolished by an ETA receptor antagonist, indicating that endothelin-1 mediates autoantibody-driven blood pressure elevation in this rat model rather than in human pre-eclampsia.
limitations: Rat AT1-AA infusion model of placental-ischaemia-like hypertension, not human pre-eclampsia
ETA antagonism is systemic, so the fall in pressure need not reflect the placental or renal ET-1 increases reported
Short 7-day exposure and small group sizes; proteinuria and other maternal end-organ endpoints not reported in the abstract

claims.text: Low-dose TNF-alpha infused for two weeks at mid-gestation in pregnant baboons (Papio hamadryas) raised systolic and diastolic blood pressure and produced proteinuria, with elevated plasma sFlt-1 and increased placental sFlt-1 and soluble endoglin expression; neither saline-treated pregnant animals nor non-pregnant TNF-alpha-treated animals developed the phenotype. This is a non-human primate model, not human pre-eclampsia.
limitations: Non-human primate model with exogenous cytokine infusion; it reproduces features of pre-eclampsia but is not human disease
Abstract reports no group sizes or effect magnitudes, and animal numbers in baboon studies are typically very small
Exogenous TNF-alpha dosing does not establish that endogenous TNF-alpha reaches causal levels in human pre-eclampsia

claims.text: In a case-control study of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotypes, mothers with the KIR AA genotype (lacking most or all activating KIR) carrying a fetus with an HLA-C2 group allele had a greatly increased risk of pre-eclampsia, and the effect did not depend on non-self or missing-self recognition.
limitations: Genotype association study; abstract reports no effect sizes or confidence intervals
Case-control design cannot establish that the receptor-ligand pair causes the syndrome
Population composition and pre-eclampsia definition not given in the abstract

claims.text: Refining the KIR AA association, maternal KIR AA frequencies were raised in affected pregnancies only when the fetus carried more HLA-C2 genes than the mother, consistent with a deleterious allogeneic effect of paternally inherited C2 rather than maternal KIR AA alone.
limitations: Genetic association; the allogeneic-effect interpretation is inferred, not directly tested
Affected pregnancies pooled across three disorders in parts of the abstract
Erratum published correcting an author name (J Clin Invest 2011;121(1):455)

claims.text: In 484 normal and 254 pre-eclamptic pregnancies in Kampala, Uganda, the combination of maternal KIR AA genotype with fetal HLA-C alleles encoding the C2 epitope was again associated with pre-eclampsia, replicating the KIR AA / fetal C2 risk combination in a sub-Saharan African population.
limitations: Single-centre genotype association study; reported odds ratio is modest (OR = 1.49)
Case-control design; no mechanistic data
Pre-eclampsia ascertainment criteria not stated in the abstract

claims.text: The protective KIR B region differs by ancestry: centromeric KIR B regions containing KIR2DS5 and KIR2DL1, unique to sub-Saharan African populations, were protective in Ugandan women, whereas telomeric KIR B genes protect Europeans, so the protective genotype is population-specific even though KIR AA is a risk factor in both.
limitations: Cross-population comparison partly against previously published European data rather than a single harmonised analysis
Protective association effect size is modest (OR = 0.59)
Genetic association only; no functional validation in this report

claims.text: Activation of KIR2DS1-expressing human decidual NK cells by HLA-C2 stimulated secretion of soluble products including GM-CSF, and GM-CSF enhanced migration of primary human trophoblast and JEG-3 trophoblast cells in vitro, giving a molecular route by which uNK recognition of trophoblast HLA-C promotes trophoblast invasion.
limitations: In vitro migration assay, not in vivo trophoblast invasion or spiral artery remodelling
Partly uses the JEG-3 choriocarcinoma cell line rather than only primary trophoblast
Cells from normal pregnancies; no comparison with pre-eclamptic decidua

claims.text: In a prospective multi-centre study of placental bed biopsies from 121 women delivered by Caesarean section for pre-eclampsia and/or fetal growth restriction versus 149 healthy controls, impaired physiological remodelling of uterine spiral arteries and associated vascular lesions were far more prevalent in the affected group (63.6% vs 10.1%).
limitations: Observational; biopsies taken at delivery so remodelling failure cannot be timed relative to disease onset
Pre-eclampsia and fetal growth restriction analysed as a combined PE/FGR group for the main comparison
Controls delivered by Caesarean section may not represent all normal pregnancies
Abstract numbers for non-remodelled arteries lacking intramural trophoblast are lost to the pipeline tag-stripping defect

claims.text: In term human placental tissue exposed to hypoxia and then reoxygenation in vitro, reactive oxygen species were generated rapidly and markers of oxidative damage (HSP72, nitrotyrosine, 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal) rose in villous endothelium and syncytiotrophoblast; ROS scavengers reduced this, showing an ischaemia-reperfusion-type insult can generate placental oxidative stress.
limitations: In vitro model of ischaemia-reperfusion in term placenta, not measured in vivo in pre-eclamptic pregnancy
Tissue from term deliveries; does not address early-gestation placentation
Whether intermittent perfusion of this magnitude occurs in human pre-eclampsia is assumed, not demonstrated

claims.text: Human placental tissue subjected to hypoxia-reoxygenation in vitro showed higher TNF-alpha mRNA than hypoxic or normoxic controls and secreted more TNF-alpha protein into the medium, so an ischaemia-reperfusion-type insult to the placenta increases placental TNF-alpha output.
limitations: In vitro hypoxia-reoxygenation model of term placenta, not human pre-eclamptic placenta in vivo
Tissue TNF-alpha protein did not differ between groups; only medium levels rose
Does not establish that circulating placental TNF-alpha is raised in pre-eclamptic women

claims.text: Conditioned medium from human placental tissue exposed to hypoxia-reoxygenation increased E-selectin expression by human umbilical vein endothelial cells, and anti-TNF-alpha antibodies significantly reduced that activation, identifying placenta-derived TNF-alpha as a mediator linking placental ischaemia to maternal endothelial activation.
limitations: HUVECs are fetal venous endothelium, an imperfect surrogate for maternal systemic endothelium
Antibody neutralisation reduced but did not abolish activation, so other placental factors contribute
In vitro only; no maternal vascular or clinical outcome measured
Orchestrator re-coded predicate from activates to contributes_to: E-selectin induction in HUVEC is a proxy for endothelial activation, not maternal endothelial dysfunction in vivo

claims.text: Administration of sFlt-1 to pregnant rats induced glomerular endotheliosis together with hypertension and proteinuria.
limitations: Rat overexpression model; not human pre-eclampsia
Dose and route may not reflect human placental sFlt-1 kinetics
Abstract only; renal histology methods not inspected

claims.text: Higher circulating sFlt-1 in pre-eclampsia was associated with lower free VEGF and PlGF, and pre-eclamptic serum produced endothelial dysfunction in vitro that exogenous VEGF and PlGF rescued.
limitations: In vitro endothelial assay; maternal vascular function in vivo not measured
Rescue by VEGF/PlGF implicates sFlt-1 antagonism indirectly; other serum factors not excluded in the abstract
Small case series; abstract only

evidenceItems.summary: Placental sFlt-1, an antagonist of VEGF-A and PlGF, is upregulated in pre-eclamptic placentas with correspondingly raised systemic sFlt-1 levels that fall after delivery.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human placental tissue and serum from women with pre-eclampsia versus normotensive pregnancy (sample sizes not stated in abstract)

evidenceItems.summary: Exogenous sFlt-1 given to pregnant rats produces hypertension together with proteinuria and glomerular endotheliosis, reproducing the maternal phenotype of pre-eclampsia.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Pregnant rats given adenoviral/recombinant sFlt-1 (sFlt-1 overexpression model); not human pre-eclampsia

evidenceItems.summary: In a nested case-control study of nulliparous women, serum sFlt-1 rose about five weeks before the clinical onset of pre-eclampsia, so the increase precedes the syndrome.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Nested case-control study within the Calcium for Preeclampsia Prevention trial: 120 matched pairs of nulliparous women, 655 serial serum specimens

evidenceItems.summary: Reduced circulating free PlGF, alongside increased sFlt-1, precedes and predicts the later development of pre-eclampsia in nulliparous women.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Nested case-control study within the Calcium for Preeclampsia Prevention trial: 120 matched pairs of nulliparous women, 655 serial serum specimens

evidenceItems.summary: Reduced oxygen tension selectively increases sFlt-1 mRNA and sFlt-1 secretion in primary human cytotrophoblasts, but not in umbilical vein endothelial cells or villous fibroblasts, linking placental hypoxia to antiangiogenic output.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Primary human cytotrophoblast culture under reduced oxygen, with HUVECs and villous fibroblasts as comparators (ELISA, real-time PCR)

evidenceItems.summary: Soluble endoglin administered to pregnant rats causes vascular permeability and hypertension, and when co-administered with sFlt-1 produces a severe pre-eclampsia phenotype including HELLP and fetal growth restriction.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Pregnant rats given adenoviral soluble endoglin alone or with sFlt-1; supporting in vitro capillary tube-formation and TGF-beta signalling assays

evidenceItems.summary: Circulating soluble endoglin rises two to three months before the clinical onset of pre-eclampsia and, together with a rising sFlt-1:PlGF ratio, marks women who later develop the syndrome.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Nested case-control study in the Calcium for Preeclampsia Prevention trial: 72 preterm pre-eclampsia cases plus 480 women across term pre-eclampsia, gestational hypertension, SGA and normotensive control groups

evidenceItems.summary: The placental (fetal-genome) C allele of the FLT1 enhancer variant rs4769613 is associated with pre-eclampsia in two Estonian cohorts, replicating the fetal-genome GWAS signal near FLT1; maternal and paternal genotypes were not associated.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Placental genotyping in two Estonian cohorts (HAPPY PREGNANCY 44 pre-eclampsia vs 1724 controls; REPROMETA 52/277) with meta-analysis of 96 cases and 2001 controls

evidenceItems.summary: In a prospective cohort of 3968 mother-child pairs, fetal-genome variants from the pre-eclampsia GWAS, including FLT1 enhancer SNPs, were associated with higher maternal serum sFLT1 and sFLT1:PlGF at 36 weeks and a steeper third-trimester rise, with effects specific to or stronger in the fetal genome.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Prospective nulliparous cohort (3968 mother-child pairs) relating maternal and fetal genotype to serial maternal sFLT1 and sFLT1:PlGF at 12, 20, 28 and 36 weeks

evidenceItems.summary: Both early- and late-onset pre-eclampsia show raised plasma sFlt-1 and reduced PlGF, but the angiogenic-factor disturbance is markedly less pronounced in late-onset (term) disease, qualifying the antiangiogenic axis as a uniform explanation.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Cross-sectional plasma study of non-pregnant women, early (24-32 weeks) and late (36-42 weeks) pregnant controls, and early-onset (<32 weeks) and late-onset (>35 weeks) pre-eclampsia cases

evidenceItems.summary: In a prospective controlled antepartum renal biopsy series, glomerular endotheliosis was present in every woman with pre-eclampsia (and also in every woman with gestational hypertension).
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human antepartum renal biopsies (light/electron microscopy, immunofluorescence); 36 hypertensive pregnant women and 12 healthy pregnant controls, Lund, Sweden

evidenceItems.summary: The same biopsy series found endotheliosis in 5 of 12 normotensive pregnant controls and in non-proteinuric gestational hypertension; the authors conclude the lesion is not pathognomonic for pre-eclampsia, differing between groups mainly in degree.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human antepartum renal biopsies; 36 hypertensive pregnant women and 12 healthy pregnant controls

evidenceItems.summary: In a prospective cohort, podocyturia (podocin-positive cultured urinary cells) at ~27 weeks was present in all women who later developed pre-eclampsia and in none of the normotensive or gestational-hypertension women, i.e. podocyte shedding preceded clinical disease and proteinuria.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human prospective longitudinal cohort (n=315 enrolled; analysed 15 PE, 15 gestational hypertension, 44 matched normotensive), urine sediment podocin staining

evidenceItems.summary: In women with pre-eclampsia, urinary soluble nephrin tracked proteinuria and urinary podocyte-specific mRNA (podocin, nephrin), suggesting proteinuria is accompanied by renal podocyte loss.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human serial urine samples: 38 samples from 9 PE women and 45 from 27 normotensive women; urinary nephrin ELISA and urinary pellet podocin/nephrin mRNA by qPCR

evidenceItems.summary: In a gestational-age-matched retrospective cohort, sFlt-1/PlGF ratios were highest in pre-eclampsia complicated by HELLP syndrome compared with isolated PE and isolated HELLP.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human retrospective single-centre cohort, 244 women (PE, PE+HELLP n=42, isolated HELLP n=7), 2011-2018, ISSHP 2014 definitions

evidenceItems.summary: Isolated HELLP syndrome without hypertension/proteinuria showed the lowest sFlt-1 and sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, suggesting HELLP is not uniformly driven by the antiangiogenic state and may be a partly distinct entity.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human retrospective single-centre cohort; isolated HELLP n=7 matched 1:2 by gestational age

evidenceItems.summary: Women with preterm eclampsia had a more severe antiangiogenic state (lower PlGF and lower PlGF/sFlt-1 ratio) than women with severe pre-eclampsia; the difference was not seen at term.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human cross-sectional study: 40 uncomplicated pregnancies, 50 severe pre-eclampsia, 35 eclampsia; maternal serum PlGF and sFlt-1 immunoassays

evidenceItems.summary: About one-third of women with term eclampsia had a normal angiogenic profile, so eclampsia (cerebral involvement) can occur without the circulating antiangiogenic imbalance, especially at term.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human cross-sectional study; term eclampsia n=15

evidenceItems.summary: In women with severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia undergoing brain imaging, eclampsia was the independent predictor of PRES (vasogenic subcortical oedema), present in 9 of 12 eclamptic women.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human single-centre retrospective imaging cohort, 53 women with severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, AIIMS Rishikesh 2018-2021

evidenceItems.summary: In a prospective study, early-onset intrauterine growth restriction (as well as early-onset PE) showed lower PlGF and higher sFlt-1 than controls, pointing to a shared placental disorder, though changes were more pronounced in pre-eclampsia.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human prospective case-control study: 76 PE, 37 isolated IUGR (early/late onset), 40 controls; plasma PlGF, sFlt-1, VCAM-1 and uterine artery Doppler

evidenceItems.summary: In a case-control comparison of 25 pre-eclamptic women with 12 normotensive pregnant women and 10 pregnant women with essential hypertension, circulating immunoglobulin with agonistic activity at the AT1 receptor was detected in every pre-eclamptic patient and in none of the controls, and the activity fell after delivery.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human case-control study (25 pre-eclamptic, 12 normotensive pregnant, 10 pregnant essential hypertension); patient IgG assayed by chronotropic response of cultured neonatal rat cardiomyocytes

evidenceItems.summary: The stimulatory activity of pre-eclamptic patient IgG was abolished by peptides corresponding to the second extracellular loop of the AT1 receptor, indicating that the autoantibodies act as direct epitope-specific agonists at the AT1 receptor in vitro (effect blocked by the protein kinase C inhibitor calphostin C).
evidenceItems.studySystem: In vitro: purified IgG from pre-eclamptic patients applied to cultured neonatal rat cardiomyocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells, with receptor-specific antagonists and epitope peptides

evidenceItems.summary: Passive transfer of total IgG or affinity-purified AT1-AA from women with pre-eclampsia into pregnant mice reproduced hypertension, proteinuria, glomerular endotheliosis, placental abnormalities and reduced fetal size, and these features were prevented by the AT1 receptor antagonist losartan or by a neutralising epitope-peptide antibody; this is a mouse passive-transfer model, not human pre-eclampsia.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Animal experiment: pregnant mice injected with total IgG or affinity-purified AT1-AA from women with pre-eclampsia, with losartan and neutralising peptide-antibody co-injection controls

evidenceItems.summary: In a prospective gestational-age-matched nested case-control study (30 pre-eclamptic, 30 normotensive pregnant women) AT1-AA were detected in only 70% of pre-eclamptic women and were also present in about 20% of normotensive pregnant controls, sFlt-1 discriminated better overall, and AT1-AA performed best for late-onset rather than early-onset disease.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human prospective nested case-control study, 30 women with pre-eclampsia and 30 gestational-age-matched normotensive pregnant women; AT1-AA bioassay plus sFlt-1 and anti-parvovirus B19 IgG

evidenceItems.summary: In a gestational-age- and parity-matched case-control study (25 severe pre-eclampsia, 25 chronic hypertension, 25 healthy pregnant controls), urinary excretion of the terminal complement complex C5b-9 was present in nearly all women with severe pre-eclampsia but almost absent in both control groups, with C3a and C5a also raised in urine, indicating complement dysregulation in severe pre-eclampsia beyond that of hypertensive pregnancy generally.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human single-centre case-control study (Brigham and Women's Hospital, 2012-2013), n=75; urine and plasma C3a, C5a and C5b-9 by ELISA

evidenceItems.summary: In 86 women assessed at 23-25 weeks' gestation, brachial artery flow-mediated dilation was markedly lower in the ten women who later developed pre-eclampsia than in women with normal outcome, so impaired maternal endothelial function is detectable before the clinical syndrome appears.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human prospective observational study: 86 women at 23-25 weeks' gestation stratified by uterine artery Doppler, brachial artery flow-mediated dilation and plasma ADMA, followed to outcome

evidenceItems.summary: Plasma concentrations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, the endogenous inhibitor of endothelial nitric oxide synthase and therefore a marker of reduced nitric oxide bioavailability, were raised in women with impaired placental perfusion and were associated with impaired endothelial function in some women, which the authors read as a potential contributory factor for pre-eclampsia.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human prospective observational study: plasma ADMA and brachial artery flow-mediated dilation at 23-25 weeks' gestation in 86 women followed to outcome

evidenceItems.summary: In a small study of 32 normal and 28 hypertensive or pre-eclamptic pregnancies, brachial artery flow-mediated dilation in the third trimester was not reduced (indeed numerically greater) in hypertensive pregnancies despite raised hsCRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha, and no inflammatory marker correlated with flow-mediated dilation, contradicting a uniform brachial endothelial deficit in hypertensive pregnancy.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human observational study: 32 normal pregnancies versus 28 pregnancies complicated by hypertensive disorder or pre-eclampsia, brachial artery flow-mediated dilation plus hsCRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha during pregnancy and at least 3 months postpartum

evidenceItems.summary: Chronic infusion of purified AT1-AA into normal pregnant rats raised mean arterial pressure and increased renal cortical and placental endothelin-1, and the hypertension was abolished by an ETA receptor antagonist, indicating that endothelin-1 mediates autoantibody-driven blood pressure elevation in this rat model rather than in human pre-eclampsia.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Animal experiment: normal pregnant rats given 7-day chronic infusion of purified rat AT1-AA, with and without an ETA receptor antagonist; renal cortical and placental ET-1 measured

evidenceItems.summary: Low-dose TNF-alpha infused for two weeks at mid-gestation in pregnant baboons (Papio hamadryas) raised systolic and diastolic blood pressure and produced proteinuria, with elevated plasma sFlt-1 and increased placental sFlt-1 and soluble endoglin expression; neither saline-treated pregnant animals nor non-pregnant TNF-alpha-treated animals developed the phenotype. This is a non-human primate model, not human pre-eclampsia.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Animal experiment: pregnant baboons (Papio hamadryas) given low-dose TNF-alpha for 2 weeks at mid-gestation, with pregnant saline and non-pregnant TNF-alpha controls; radiotelemetric blood pressure, proteinuria, plasma sFlt-1, placental sFlt-1 and sEng mRNA

evidenceItems.summary: In a case-control study of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotypes, mothers with the KIR AA genotype (lacking most or all activating KIR) carrying a fetus with an HLA-C2 group allele had a greatly increased risk of pre-eclampsia, and the effect did not depend on non-self or missing-self recognition.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human maternal-fetal genotype case-control study (maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C typing in pre-eclamptic and control pregnancies)

evidenceItems.summary: Refining the KIR AA association, maternal KIR AA frequencies were raised in affected pregnancies only when the fetus carried more HLA-C2 genes than the mother, consistent with a deleterious allogeneic effect of paternally inherited C2 rather than maternal KIR AA alone.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human maternal and fetal genotyping across pregnancy-disorder cohorts (pre-eclampsia, fetal growth restriction, recurrent miscarriage) with trophoblast HLA-C surface staining

evidenceItems.summary: In 484 normal and 254 pre-eclamptic pregnancies in Kampala, Uganda, the combination of maternal KIR AA genotype with fetal HLA-C alleles encoding the C2 epitope was again associated with pre-eclampsia, replicating the KIR AA / fetal C2 risk combination in a sub-Saharan African population.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotyping in 484 normal and 254 pre-eclamptic pregnancies, Mulago Hospital, Kampala, Uganda

evidenceItems.summary: The protective KIR B region differs by ancestry: centromeric KIR B regions containing KIR2DS5 and KIR2DL1, unique to sub-Saharan African populations, were protective in Ugandan women, whereas telomeric KIR B genes protect Europeans, so the protective genotype is population-specific even though KIR AA is a risk factor in both.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotyping in a Ugandan cohort compared with reported European associations

evidenceItems.summary: Activation of KIR2DS1-expressing human decidual NK cells by HLA-C2 stimulated secretion of soluble products including GM-CSF, and GM-CSF enhanced migration of primary human trophoblast and JEG-3 trophoblast cells in vitro, giving a molecular route by which uNK recognition of trophoblast HLA-C promotes trophoblast invasion.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human primary decidual NK cells and primary trophoblast plus JEG-3 trophoblast cell line, in vitro (microarray, intracellular FACS, ELISA, migration assays)

evidenceItems.summary: In a prospective multi-centre study of placental bed biopsies from 121 women delivered by Caesarean section for pre-eclampsia and/or fetal growth restriction versus 149 healthy controls, impaired physiological remodelling of uterine spiral arteries and associated vascular lesions were far more prevalent in the affected group (63.6% vs 10.1%).
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human placental bed biopsies obtained at Caesarean section; prospective multi-centre observational cohort (121 PE/FGR, 149 controls)

evidenceItems.summary: In term human placental tissue exposed to hypoxia and then reoxygenation in vitro, reactive oxygen species were generated rapidly and markers of oxidative damage (HSP72, nitrotyrosine, 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal) rose in villous endothelium and syncytiotrophoblast; ROS scavengers reduced this, showing an ischaemia-reperfusion-type insult can generate placental oxidative stress.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Term human placental tissue explants subjected to hypoxia-reoxygenation in vitro (fluorogenic ROS probe, immunolocalisation, scavenger pre-loading)

evidenceItems.summary: Human placental tissue subjected to hypoxia-reoxygenation in vitro showed higher TNF-alpha mRNA than hypoxic or normoxic controls and secreted more TNF-alpha protein into the medium, so an ischaemia-reperfusion-type insult to the placenta increases placental TNF-alpha output.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human placental tissue explants subjected to hypoxia-reoxygenation in vitro, with conditioned medium transfer to HUVECs

evidenceItems.summary: Conditioned medium from human placental tissue exposed to hypoxia-reoxygenation increased E-selectin expression by human umbilical vein endothelial cells, and anti-TNF-alpha antibodies significantly reduced that activation, identifying placenta-derived TNF-alpha as a mediator linking placental ischaemia to maternal endothelial activation.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Conditioned medium from hypoxia-reoxygenation-treated human placental explants applied to human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) in vitro, with TNF-alpha neutralisation

evidenceItems.summary: Administration of sFlt-1 to pregnant rats induced glomerular endotheliosis together with hypertension and proteinuria.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Pregnant rats given exogenous sFlt-1 (adenoviral overexpression); not human pre-eclampsia

evidenceItems.summary: Higher circulating sFlt-1 in pre-eclampsia was associated with lower free VEGF and PlGF, and pre-eclamptic serum produced endothelial dysfunction in vitro that exogenous VEGF and PlGF rescued.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Serum from women with pre-eclampsia tested in an in vitro endothelial assay
